purpose: Bounded GAO-26-107120 route from disability-related care need through physical, sensory, communication, digital, and bias barriers and federal oversight, preserving completed-care and health-outcome gaps.

events.geography: United States health-care system and HHS oversight; 12 HHS surveys and nongeneralizable survey of 1,194 adults with disabilities
events.date_precision: GAO report published December 19, 2025; literature 2013–2024 and HHS oversight/recommendation status at publication
events.denominator: One in four U.S. adults reports a disability as a broad frame; GAO survey sample 1,194 adults with disabilities; barrier and oversight bases vary
events.method: GAO literature and rule review, analysis of 12 HHS population-health surveys, nongeneralizable disability survey, stakeholder interviews, and CMS/OCR/HHS oversight review
events.missingness: Encounter-level need, accommodation request/receipt, provider equipment, appointment completion, delay, avoided care, treatment continuity, work/family time, health outcome, complaint resolution, and provider exit are not linked
events.exposure: Disability-related physical, sensory, communication, cognitive, digital, and provider-interaction barriers are identified across literature, stakeholder evidence, and selected survey material
events.alternatives_before_action: Alternative providers, equipment, interpreters, quiet settings, digital/phone routes, family assistance, transport, and ability to switch are not observed for the same patient
events.immediate_burden_or_benefit: Potential barriers include inaccessible exam equipment, kiosks/apps, sensory environments, communication, provider assumptions, and denied services; the review does not estimate national barrier prevalence
events.choice_or_response: CMS inspections, OCR complaints/compliance reviews, HHS accessibility requirements, and five GAO recommendations are visible institutional routes; completed care or patient correction is not verified
events.person_or_actor_with_control: Providers, health systems, CMS, OCR, HHS, patients, and family supporters control different parts of the interface; no encounter-level authority or choice condition is retained
events.remedy_or_institutional_response: HHS amended accessibility requirements in 2024, but GAO found no detailed strategic plan/timeline and limited public aggregation of oversight results; recommendations remained open at publication
events.immediate_outcome: The record establishes an accessibility and measurement gap between nominal coverage/provider capacity and usable care
events.protected_outcome: Accessible equipment, communication, and accommodation could protect safe treatment continuity, but successful completion is not observed
events.sacrificed_outcome: Extra time, family coordination, failed encounters, delayed diagnosis, or avoided care may shift cost and risk to patients, but no patient-level sacrifice is measured
events.cost_risk_transfer: The review does not identify whether accessibility costs transfer among patients, families, providers, insurers, or public oversight systems
events.later_outcome: No linked health, work, household-time, trust, complaint, provider switching, or exit outcome is observed
events.meaning_and_attribution: Bias, dignity, fairness, and trust concerns are identified as possible mechanisms, but patient interpretation and attribution are not measured
events.public_or_collective_response: Federal recommendations and oversight routes are observed; patient organizing, complaint resolution, policy response, and collective action are not linked
events.counterexample: A barrier identified in literature or stakeholder evidence may be successfully accommodated in a particular encounter; nominal equipment or coverage does not prove either failure or success
events.source_and_uncertainty: GAO review and nongeneralizable evidence; no national barrier prevalence, causal health estimate, or encounter-level remedy result is established

arrows.to: physical, sensory, communication, cognitive, digital, or bias barrier
arrows.evidence: GAO identifies these barrier domains through literature, stakeholder evidence, selected survey material, and oversight review
arrows.counterexample: Barrier domains are not a national prevalence estimate and may be absent or successfully accommodated in a particular encounter
arrows.remaining_gap: Patient-level need, provider, requested accommodation, encounter, and completion record

arrows.to: failed, delayed, avoided, or extra-burden care encounter
arrows.evidence: The review describes inaccessible equipment, communication, sensory environments, digital interfaces, and provider interaction concerns but does not count failed or avoided encounters nationally
arrows.counterexample: A provider or family member may supply an accommodation, and a described barrier may not affect a specific encounter
arrows.remaining_gap: Encounter completion, wait/delay, extra travel/time, family assistance, and care avoidance

arrows.to: provider correction and restored usable care
arrows.evidence: CMS/OCR oversight and five GAO recommendations are visible, but HHS did not have detailed execution timelines and OCR results were not routinely shared in aggregate
arrows.counterexample: Individual voluntary correction may occur without public aggregation, while a public recommendation may not change a patient encounter
arrows.remaining_gap: Provider implementation, accommodation receipt, correction, repeat encounter, and safe continuity

arrows.to: health, work, family-time, and household-security outcome
arrows.evidence: The GAO record contains no linked encounter-level treatment, delayed diagnosis, health, work, or family-burden follow-up
arrows.counterexample: Health outcomes can be shaped by disease, treatment, coverage, and household resources apart from accessibility
arrows.remaining_gap: Same-patient treatment continuity, safety, health, work/care time, financial cost, and recovery

arrows.to: trust, complaint, provider switching, collective action, or exit
arrows.evidence: The review identifies complaint and oversight routes but does not link a patient encounter to resolution, trust change, switching, or exit
arrows.counterexample: Low complaint visibility may reflect low awareness, burden, or distrust rather than low harm; complaint filing also does not prove correction
arrows.remaining_gap: Patient-reported experience, complaint effort, response, remedy, trust, repeat use, switching, and exit

boundary: This ledger formalizes a health-care accessibility and oversight stage beneath formal coverage or provider availability. It does not establish barrier prevalence, failed-care rates, accommodation receipt, health outcomes, family burden, remedy, trust, or exit.
storage_boundary: Only GAO-published review findings, oversight stages, recommendation status, and interpretation limits are retained; HHS survey files, provider records, and OCR/CMS administrative files are not stored.
